sections.overview: Plathemis lydia is a widespread North American dragonfly in the skimmer family Libellulidae.
sections.identification: Mature males have a chalky white abdomen and broad dark bands across the wings; females are brown with pale side markings and three dark spots on each wing.
sections.habitat: It breeds around lakes, ponds and slow streams, often where the bottom is muddy.
sections.diet: Adults catch small insects in flight.
sections.behavior: It perches low in open places; males defend waterside territories.
sections.reproduction: Females tap eggs into water or wet mud near vegetation; males may guard them.
sections.ecology: The aquatic larvae develop in freshwater and tolerate a range of water conditions.
sections.conservation: The Illinois agency describes it as common and native in that state.
